questions.question: On a slippery road, you should keep a following distance that is:
questions.explanation: You need more distance to stop on a slippery road. Always increase your following distance when roads are slippery.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a traffic light that is not working?

options.text: Stop completely and yield the right-of-way before entering.
You don't need to stop if the intersection is clear.
Drive quickly through to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and yield the right-of-way before entering.
questions.explanation: Treat a broken traffic light like an all-way stop. Come to a complete stop, look, and yield the right-of-way before entering the intersection.

questions.question: If your tire blows out, you should:

options.text: Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.
questions.explanation: Take your foot off the gas and let the car slow down. Use light braking only after the vehicle has slowed down a lot.

questions.question: A solid yellow arrow on a traffic light means:

options.text: Speed up to make the turn before the light changes.
You don't need to signal your turn.
Get ready to stop and yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get ready to stop and yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the green arrow is ending soon. Be ready to stop and let oncoming traffic go before you turn.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights, you should:

options.text: Drive around the gates if you don't see a train.
Stop well behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, then go when the gates rise.
Slow down and drive around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop well behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, then go when the gates rise.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when warned by signs, lights, or a flagperson. It is illegal to drive around lowered gates.

questions.question: Work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs are used to:

options.text: Keep traffic away from dangerous work areas.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep traffic away from dangerous work areas.
questions.explanation: Work zones are dangerous for workers and drivers. Watch for cones, barrels, signs, large vehicles, and workers in bright vests. They warn you and show you where to go.

questions.question: After drinking several beers, the only way to reduce alcohol's effects is:
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Coffee, exercise, or cold showers won't speed this up. It takes about one hour per drink.

questions.question: If a truck or bus is turning right where you also need to turn right, you should:

options.text: Wait until the truck or bus finishes turning.
Squeeze between it and the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the truck or bus finishes turning.
questions.explanation: Don't try to fit between a turning truck or bus and the curb. You could crash. Wait until it completes its turn before you turn.

questions.question: Only ____ can lower blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
questions.explanation: Your body needs time to remove alcohol from your system. Eating, drinking, or anything else cannot speed up this process.

questions.question: Which substances can make it unsafe to drive?

options.text: Cough syrups and cold medicines with codeine or antihistamines.

questions.explanation: Many drugs affect your driving ability. These include prescription depressants, over-the-counter cough and cold medicines, allergy medications, and illegal drugs.

questions.question: You can identify an aggressive driver by:
questions.explanation: Watch for drivers making unsafe or careless lane changes. Don't challenge them. The safest action is to stay away from aggressive drivers.

questions.question: If you see an aggressive driver, you should:
questions.explanation: The safest choice is to get out of their way. Never compete with other drivers. Respect all road users.

questions.question: The amount of alcohol in the blood is called:
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures the percentage of alcohol in your blood. A higher BAC means more impairment.

questions.question: If you drive faster than others on a two-lane road and pass many cars, you will:

options.text: Get to your destination faster and safer.
Increase your chances of a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your chances of a crash.
questions.explanation: Avoid passing on two-lane roads. Each time you pass a car, your crash risk goes up.

questions.question: If you feel drowsy while driving, you should:
questions.explanation: Pull over at a rest stop to take a nap, stretch, or switch drivers. Don't rely on caffeine pills or energy drinks. Only real rest is safe.

questions.question: Which of the following is dangerous in a work zone?

options.text: Not watching carefully for workers and equipment

questions.explanation: In a work zone, slow down for traffic and keep a safe distance from other vehicles. Watch carefully for workers and equipment.

questions.question: Where should children age 12 and under ride in a vehicle with airbags?

options.text: The bed of a pickup truck

questions.explanation: Airbags can hurt children. Children age 12 and under should always sit in the back seat of a vehicle with airbags.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells drivers that the right lane is ending. Be ready for cars to merge into your lane.

questions.question: You must yield to a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog:

options.text: Only when the guide dog is leading the person across the street
Only if a crossing guard is present

questions.explanation: Always give the right-of-way to pedestrians with guide dogs or white canes.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the center line mean?
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line on your side means you cannot pass. Solid yellow lines show where passing is not safe.

questions.question: When driving behind a large truck on the freeway, you should:

options.text: Follow closer than you would a passenger vehicle
Follow farther back than you would a passenger vehicle
Move to the right side of the truck and wait to pass

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow farther back than you would a passenger vehicle
questions.explanation: Stay farther back from large trucks because they have large blind spots where the driver cannot see you.

questions.question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?
questions.explanation: Alcohol and drugs slow your nervous system. They reduce alertness, increase reaction time, and harm coordination.

questions.question: If a tire blows out while driving, you should:

options.text: Hold the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and leave the traffic lane
Brake hard and steer toward the right edge of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and leave the traffic lane
questions.explanation: Stay calm. Hold the steering wheel tight and take your foot off the gas. Let the car slow down. Apply the brakes gently when safe. Don't move to the shoulder until the car has slowed a lot.

questions.question: What is the purpose of rumble strips?

options.text: They alert drivers to tire problems
They test a vehicle's shock absorbers
They warn drowsy drivers with vibration and noise when they leave the road

questions.correctAnswerText: They warn drowsy drivers with vibration and noise when they leave the road
questions.explanation: Rumble strips make noise and vibration to warn tired or distracted drivers that they are leaving the road or approaching a stop sign or light.

questions.question: Which of the following commonly causes traffic crashes?

options.text: Speeding or driving too fast for conditions
Getting enough rest and staying alert
Paying attention and focusing on driving

questions.correctAnswerText: Speeding or driving too fast for conditions
questions.explanation: Speeding and driving too fast for conditions cause many crashes. Always drive at legal speeds and adjust your speed for road and weather conditions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign shows there is a pedestrian crosswalk ahead.

questions.question: You see pedestrians near the road. What should you do?

options.text: Sound your horn and maintain your speed
Speed up to leave the area quickly
Slow down and pass with caution

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and pass with caution
questions.explanation: When you see pedestrians near the road, slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Reserved parking for people with disabilities

questions.explanation: This sign warns that two lanes going the same direction will soon become one lane.

questions.question: If you are getting tired while driving, you should:

options.text: Stop and rest or let someone else drive

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest or let someone else drive
questions.explanation: To avoid drowsy driving, take breaks every hour on long trips. If possible, share driving with another person so you can both rest.

questions.question: When taking any medicine, you should:

options.text: Ask your doctor about effects on driving before you drive
Keep your window open and drive slowly

questions.correctAnswerText: Ask your doctor about effects on driving before you drive
questions.explanation: Both prescription and over-the-counter medicines can affect your driving. Always ask your doctor or pharmacist how a medicine might affect your ability to drive.
